title: Bohr–Sommerfeld Asymptotics for Limit-Circle Jacobi Matrices
description:
A Jacobi matrix whose off-diagonal entries grow regularly like \(c\,n^\alpha\) with \(\alpha>1\), without a strong alternation between even and odd entries, is in the limit-circle case: it has a one-parameter family of self-adjoint extensions \(H_t\), each with discrete spectrum. The growth of the eigenvalue counting function is known up to multiplicative constants, but no eigenvalue law with an explicit constant was known beyond a few explicitly solvable chains. We prove such a law, with an explicit offset, for every self-adjoint extension of a zero-diagonal Jacobi matrix with links \(a_n=c\,n^\alpha(1+(\kappa+\kappa'(-1)^n)/n+O(n^{-1-\delta}))\) in the limit-circle range \(2|\kappa'|<\alpha-1\). For \(\kappa'=0\) the eigenvalues satisfy the Bohr–Sommerfeld rule \(N_{\lambda_j} I_\alpha-\kappa\pi/(2\alpha)=j\pi+t+O(j^{-\min(1,\delta)})\), where \(N_\lambda=(\lambda/2c)^{1/\alpha}\) and \(I_\alpha= frac12\mathrm{B}( frac{\alpha-1}{2\alpha}, frac12)\), with no quarter-period correction in the normalisation of the extensions fixed by the solutions at \(\lambda=0\), and for a shifted power with a curvature term the next coefficient is \((\kappa_2+(2\alpha-1)/24)\,J_\alpha\). For \(\kappa' eq0\) (dimerised links) the far field is a Bessel problem of order \( u= frac12-\kappa'/(\alpha-1)\): measured in units of \(\pi\), the offsets of the two extensions \(H_0\) and \(H_{\pi/2}\) are shifted by \(+\kappa'/(2(\alpha-1))\) and \(-\kappa'/(2(\alpha-1))\) from the balanced values \(0\) and \( frac12\), every other extension follows one of these two laws, and the remainder is \(o(1)\).

The proofs combine an exact rotation identity for two-site blocks, an adiabatic normal form, a Bessel comparison for the far field, and a discrete Olver-type bound for Airy approximations that we prove from scratch; the last also extends a theorem of Fischer, Burgarth and Lonigro on singular limits from \(\alpha>4/3\) to \(\alpha>1\). Applications include the spectra of all symmetry-preserving self-adjoint extensions of higher-order squeezing operators and the Krein and Friedrichs spectra of birth–death processes with polynomial rates. For these processes we compute the critical indices of Berg and Szwarc exactly: \((1- u)/2\) for the Friedrichs solution and \((1+ u)/2\) for every other N-extremal solution, all of them determinate at the critical weight. The numerical claims are checked against an independent eigenvalue computation.
